findings: The CutFibers dependency encodes actual complete cut sets. collapseCuts takes the finite image under the proved collapse; localCuts filters precisely the two physical preimages of s. expandCuts restores every nonduplicate core cut inside the actual interval and exactly the chosen Q. Its inverse proofs use the singleton fibers away from s and the proved existence of an in-interval lift; they do not assume a cut-list correspondence. Canonical cutSetEquiv transports this to actual ordered compositions, including the unary composition.

CutFiberCondition retains all necessary endpoint conditions: selected local occurrences lie inside I, selection is nonempty exactly when s belongs to the complete core cut set, and any endpoint collapsing to s is mandatory. The new iff lemmas simplify this actual condition rather than replacing it with a freely assumed abstract cardinality.

cutSubsetPair_cases derives all four subsets of the distinct positions A and B. cutFiberCondition_empty proves that the empty subset is valid exactly when s is absent from C, including the impossibility of an endpoint collapsing to an absent mandatory core cut. emptyCutFiberEquiv constructs a true one-element fiber, so no-core-cut sums have exactly one term, without assuming two or more parts.

For strict spanning endpoints, the endpoint obligations are proved impossible from strict inequalities and the exact two-point collapse fiber. If s is a core cut, nonemptiness removes only the empty subset and leaves precisely A-only, B-only and both. spanningRowsEquiv proves distinctness using actual A/B membership and A_lt_B, and surjectivity from the exact iff classification. It is not merely a count of an unverified list.

At an interval starting at A, core endpoint membership derives s in C and forces A into Q. Thus A-only and both are exactly the two presentations; B-only and empty are ruled out, not silently omitted. At an interval ending at B, the proof symmetrically forces B, giving B-only and both. The right/left exterior inequalities ensure the optional other occurrence lies inside I. These assumptions are exactly the source two-presentation cases.

All four summation theorems use proved equivalences and finite sums over PUnit/Fin2/Fin3. The codomain is any AddCommMonoid, so the identities are independent of gate values, child weights, cancellations or sign assumptions. Every zero-valued summand and every composition encoded by the fixed actual core cut set remains included.

The spanning code order is A-only, B-only, both. Source aspr:three-presentations and the existing three_ordinary/three_root lemmas list B-only, A-only, both. This is a harmless permutation for the present additive sums, but the future weighted proof must use the recorded row correspondence. Starting and ending code orders already agree with the source optional-cut narrative.
